complaint.product: Payday loan, title loan, personal loan, or advance loan
complaint.narrative: I set up autopay for this loan six months ago and it worked fine until last month, when my payment was never withdrawn and I was charged a late fee as a result. I have a screenshot of my autopay settings still showing as active.

allegations: Autopay set up six months ago worked fine until last month
Payment was never withdrawn last month
Charged a late fee as a result of the missed withdrawal
extraction.account_details_mentioned: Autopay set up six months ago; customer has a screenshot of autopay settings still showing as active

account.account_note: Installment loan, current. Opened 2025-10-27. Payments due on the 27th.

transactions.note: Autopay disabled by customer via mobile app
Scheduled installment $100.00 not received; no autopay instruction active

verification.fact_verification_explanation: The customer's central allegation is that autopay was active, the company failed to withdraw the payment, and the late fee was therefore charged in error. The records confirm the events but contradict the customer's explanation for them. The 2026-03-27 and 2026-04-27 autopay withdrawals of $100 each match the customer's statement that autopay worked until last month. The 2026-05-27 installment of $100 was not received, and a $25 late fee was assessed on 2026-06-01, so the missed payment and the fee both happened. However, on 2026-05-09 the account log shows 'Autopay disabled by customer via mobile app.' The 2026-05-27 entry says 'no autopay instruction active.' The payment was therefore not withdrawn because autopay had been turned off from the customer's own app, not because of a company error. The customer's screenshot is not on file. It does not change the finding, because the system log directly contradicts the claim that autopay was active.
verification.risk_rationale: The amount is a $25 late fee, and the claim is confirmed false against clear records. There is no attorney/regulator reference, no identity-theft or fraud dispute, no misleading-terms allegation, no hardship or vulnerability indicator, no collector conduct, and no embedded instructions.

policy.topic: Fee Waiver and Goodwill Credit Authority
policy.text:
# Internal Policy: Fee Waiver and Goodwill Credit Authority

**Applies to:** Complaints where account/transaction data confirms a fee was charged in error, or where a goodwill gesture is being considered for a confirmed service failure.

## Authority thresholds
| Fee/credit amount | Who may approve |
|---|---|
| $0 – $50 | Complaints analyst, no additional sign-off required |
| $50.01 – $200 | Complaints analyst with supervisor co-sign |
| $200.01+ | Supervisor or manager approval required; analyst may not approve independently |

## When a waiver is appropriate
- The transaction history **confirms** the fee was charged in error (e.g., payment was received before the due date but a late fee was still assessed).
- The fee was charged due to a documented system or processing error.
- A documented goodwill exception for a first-time, low-dollar fee on an otherwise good-standing account (use sparingly, document the rationale).

## When a waiver is NOT appropriate
- The transaction history confirms the fee was correctly charged (no error occurred) — the response should explain the charge, not waive it.
- The complaint's underlying fact could not be verified (missing/incomplete data) — route to manual review rather than waiving preemptively.
- The complaint involves a dispute of right vs. convenience (e.g., customer disagrees with a disclosed, legitimate fee) — explain the fee and its basis; do not waive solely to end the complaint.

## What an analyst or agent may say
- May state the exact dollar amount being waived and the specific reason (tied to the confirmed error).
- May NOT waive a fee "as a one-time courtesy" without a documented rationale on file — every waiver must cite either a confirmed error or an explicit goodwill justification.

## Documentation requirement
Every waiver, regardless of amount, must be logged with: the confirming evidence (which transaction record), the dollar amount, and the approving party.

*This is an internal, generic policy created for a training/demonstration environment and does not reflect any specific company's actual policy.*

draft.draft_text:
You told us your autopay ran smoothly for months, then last month the payment never came out of your account and you ended up with a late fee. That's frustrating when you thought autopay was taking care of it, and we looked at each part of what you described.

Autopay working until last month: You're right that it worked before. Our records show $100 withdrawals on March 27 and April 27.

The payment not being withdrawn: You're also right that the $100 installment due May 27 wasn't taken. Our account log has an entry on May 9 that reads "Autopay disabled by customer via mobile app." On May 27, the log shows no autopay instruction active, and that's why no withdrawal was made that day.

The late fee: A $25 late fee was added to your account on June 1, after the May 27 installment wasn't received. Because our records don't show an error on our side, the fee is staying on your account.

You mentioned a screenshot showing autopay as active. We don't have it on file, so we haven't been able to look at it. If you'd like to send it, along with the date it was taken and anything else you think we should know, we'll review it. You're welcome to send more information at any time, and you can reply to this message or call the number on your account.

Case reference: 22853918
draft.policy_cited: 06 Fee Waiver and Goodwill Credit Authority, 'When a waiver is NOT appropriate' (records show the fee was charged without error, so the response explains the charge rather than waiving it)

Payment was never withdrawn last month
Charged a late fee as a result of the missed withdrawal

verifier.completeness_check: pass — all three allegations are addressed individually: autopay worked until last month (March 27 and April 27 withdrawals), the payment not being withdrawn (May 9 disable entry, May 27 'no autopay instruction active'), and the late fee (a $25 fee on June 1 that stays on the account).
verifier.groundedness_check: pass — the dates, the $100 installment, the $25 fee, and both log entries match the verification output. The explanation that no withdrawal was made because autopay was disabled matches the verification finding. The screenshot is described only as not on file, which the verification confirms. The phrase 'a screenshot showing autopay as active' is a small inference about the screenshot's content, but it is consistent with the verification's reference to the 'claim that autopay was active'. No refund, credit, or approval is claimed.
verifier.policy_authorization_check: pass — no remedy is offered (remedy_stated and referral_stated are null). Keeping the fee and explaining the charge is what Policy 06 prescribes under 'When a waiver is NOT appropriate' when the records confirm the fee was correctly charged.
verifier.prohibited_language_check: pass — no fault admission beyond confirmed fact, no guarantees about the future, no legal conclusions, and no promises outside documented authority. 'You're right that it worked before' and 'You're also right that the $100 installment... wasn't taken' only confirm verified facts. Nothing discourages other channels, and the invitation to send more information is not discouraging.
verifier.tone_structure_check: pass — the draft follows Policy 11 in order: a specific opening acknowledgment, findings with dates and amounts, an outcome (the fee stays, with the reason), next steps (send the screenshot or reply or call), and the case reference 22853918. It uses plain second-person language, separate short paragraphs per allegation, and no marketing content. The length is acceptable for a multi-allegation response. The outcome is folded into the late-fee paragraph rather than set apart, but it is clearly stated.
